summary: This note is a Wikipedia-style biography of James Howard Bryant, a singer, arranger and composer. It is best known for providing the singing voice of Tony, played onscreen by Richard Beymer, in the 1961 film West Side Story, though he received no screen credit. The note also lists his other film and television singing work, including Thoroughly Modern Millie, Bye Bye Birdie, and the group that performed the Batman TV theme.
one_line: James Howard Bryant is a singer, arranger and composer known for dubbing Tony's singing voice in the 1961 film West Side Story.
key_facts: James Howard Bryant was born on June 2, 1929.
James Howard Bryant is a singer, arranger and composer.
He is best known for providing the singing voice of Tony in the 1961 film musical West Side Story.
Tony was played onscreen by Richard Beymer in West Side Story.
Bryant received no screen credit for his work on West Side Story.
Bryant states that Richard Beymer was "a nice guy, and every time he did an interview he would mention my name."
Bryant sang for James Fox in the 1967 film musical Thoroughly Modern Millie.
Bryant sang in "The Telephone Hour" number in Bye Bye Birdie.
Bryant also sang in the group that performed the theme song of the TV series Batman.
